summary: Specifies IANA guidelines for allocating new values for the Routing Type field in the IPv6 Routing Header. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: It tells the keeper of the list how to hand out new numbers for kinds of routing notes in IPv6.

questions: how to get a new routing type
subtitle: How new Routing Type values for the IPv6 Routing Header get allocated by IANA.

tldr.problem: The IPv6 Routing Header has a Routing Type field, but IANA had no guidance for allocating new values for it.
tldr.mechanism: New Routing Type values are allocated through IETF Review or IESG Approval, as defined in RFC 5226.
tldr.outcome: Two experimental values, 253 and 254, are already available. The RFC does not change the security properties of the Routing Header.

today: RFC 5871 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2460. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes it.

sections.title: A Missing Allocation Rule
sections.content: This document gives the IANA guidelines for allocating new values for the Routing Type field in the IPv6 Routing Header defined in RFC 2460. The guidelines follow the format in RFC 5226. Previously, no IANA guidance existed for such allocations, and RFC 5871 updates RFC 2460 to fill that gap.
sections.eli5: There was a list of numbers but no rule for who could add to it. Now there is one.

sections.title: How Values Are Allocated
sections.content:
New Routing Type values are allocated through IETF Review or IESG Approval, as defined in RFC 5226. A new type therefore needs a published and reviewed specification, or approval from the IESG.

Two experimental values, 253 and 254, are already available for use, as set out in RFC 4727.
sections.eli5: To get a new number you have to convince the reviewers. Two numbers are kept free for people to try out ideas.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The specification does not change the security properties of the Routing Header. It does note that past experience shows it is easy to design routing headers that have significant problems, and it points to RFC 5095, which deprecated Type 0 Routing Headers in IPv6.
sections.eli5: Routing notes can be risky if designed badly, so new kinds should be looked at carefully.

references.text: Deering, S. and R. Hinden, "Internet Protocol, Version 6 (IPv6) Specification", RFC 2460, December 1998.
Narten, T. and H. Alvestrand, "Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs", BCP 26, RFC 5226, May 2008.
Fenner, B., "Experimental Values In IPv4, IPv6, ICMPv4, ICMPv6, UDP, and TCP Headers", RFC 4727, November 2006.
Abley, J., Savola, P., and G. Neville-Neil, "Deprecation of Type 0 Routing Headers in IPv6", RFC 5095, December 2007.
